does: Leaves cooked meat alone off the heat for a while, so that its juices settle and stay in when it is cut.

intro.what: Resting leaves meat off the heat before it is carved.
intro.why: It asks you to plan a pause before slicing and to notice the effect on the juices and crust.

how: Lift the meat out of the pan onto a rack or a warm plate.
Leave it uncovered, or loosely tented, somewhere warm.
Wait about as long as it took to sear a steak, and much longer for a large roast.
Pour the juices it gives up back into the sauce.

cues.text: Little juice runs out when it is sliced, and the cut face is evenly coloured.
The meat has relaxed and gives a little under a finger.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting it straight away, so that the juice floods the board and the meat eats dry.
mistakes.fix: Wait. The meat stays hot inside for longer than you think.

mistakes.mistake: Wrapping it tightly in foil, which steams the crust soft.
mistakes.fix: Leave it open, or tent the foil loosely.

quiz.question: Why rest meat before slicing it?
choices: To keep browning the meat in the cooking pan.
To trap steam tightly against the crust.
To let juices settle before slicing.
quiz.because: Resting gives juices time to settle, helping more stay in the meat when it is sliced.

quiz.question: Where does the meat go to rest in this method?
choices: Onto a rack or warm plate, away from the pan heat.
Back into the hot frying pan.
Into a tightly sealed foil parcel every time.
quiz.because: Lift the meat out of the hot pan onto a rack or warm plate for its pause off the heat.

quiz.question: Which observation is consistent with the intended result?
choices: Little juice runs out when the meat is sliced.
A crisp crust turns wet beneath tight foil.
quiz.because: Less juice running onto the board is the result this resting method aims for.

quiz.question: Tight foil has steamed the crust soft. What would you change?
choices: Seal the foil around the edges to retain more warmth.
Leave it tightly wrapped until the crust dries again.
Leave it uncovered or tent the foil loosely.
quiz.because: Tight foil traps steam against the crust. A loose tent or no cover avoids steaming it soft.

comes_after.why: Resting is how a sear ends.
